court: High Court of Judicature at Madras
trial_court: III Additional District Court, Tirunelveli - I.D.O.P.No.42 of 2019
facts_of_case: The parties were married in 2010 and had a child out of wedlock. The wife left the husband's home in 2010 and never returned. The husband filed for restitution of conjugal rights, which was later transferred to I Additional Sub Court, Madurai. The case was eventually decreed in favour of the husband. The wife failed to file her counter statement, leading to an ex parte decree.

legal_principles.principle: A party who fails to file a counter statement in time may be set ex parte.
legal_principles.held: In spite of several opportunities, the respondent / wife failed to file her counter and therefore, she was set ex parte.
applicable_acts_sections: Civil Procedure Code, 1908 — Order IX, Rule 13

legal_principles.principle: A party's intention to harass the other party is not a valid reason for setting aside an ex parte decree.
legal_principles.held: The act of the respondent / wife in filing the application for setting aside the ex parte decree is only with an intention to harass the petitioner herein.

outcome.final_order: The Civil Revision Petition is filed against the order passed in I.A.No.4 of 2023 in I.D.O.P.No.42 of 2019, dated 16.06.2023.
